title: Library Life: Pumpkin Glow, cryptozoologist visit and share the warmth

content:
While the library seems to always have something going on, this week I wanted to highlight a few of my favorite programs. Starting off, the Huntington Memorial Library has officially started our “Share The Warmth: Knit & Crochet Winter Wear Drive.” From now until Nov. 28th we will be accepting donations of handmade hats, scarves, gloves/mittens, and blankets of any size. Donations can also be brought to Sybil’s Yarn Shop in Cooperstown. In November the donations will be put on display and will be free to take by anyone in need, no questions asked.

Next, we are thrilled to have cryptozoologist Ken Gerhard returning to the library at 6 p.m. Wednesday, Oct. 21 to present another fascinating presentation: “Monsters Are Real: Mothman, Werewolves, the Chupacabra, and Other Phantom Creatures.” Attendees will explore the mysterious world of legendary creatures, from the eerie Mothman and shape-shifting werewolves to the elusive Chupacabra and other strange beings reported around the world. Discover chilling eyewitness accounts, fascinating folklore, and the enduring mysteries that keep these phantom creatures alive in our imaginations! It’s sure to be a great time and a perfect way to kick off the days leading up to Halloween.

Ariel Turrigiano is program librarian at Huntington Memorial Library. A library column appears in the community section of The Daily Star every week. Columns may also be found online at www.thedailystar.com/community/library/corner.
